# Crimes - 2001 to Present (City of Chicago): agent index

Reported incidents of crime in the City of Chicago since 2001, from the Chicago Police Department CLEAR system, published on the Chicago Data Portal (Socrata) and updated daily. Not a survey: one row per incident.

Publisher: City of Chicago, Chicago Police Department. Dataset id: `chicago-crimes`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/narr/foia/data_disclaimer.html. LLM processing: `unknown`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the year the incident occurred.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

The JSONL records are compact: `availability` maps each form (or `all`) to runs of waves, `origins` gives where each field came from as `kind:source` or `rule:name@version`, and `origins.codes` is the origin the codes share (a code lists its own when they differ). Per-wave counts and the notes on origins are left out. The full records in `metadata/` are canonical; each shard header's `full_records` names the files.

Line form: `name | waves by form | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span. `1972-1985,1987-2024 (not 1986)` means the release has a 1986 wave and the variable wasn't in it. `all 1972-1987; form A,C 1988-2024` means everyone was asked through 1987 and only forms A and C from 1988. The release's waves are: `20261119`: 2001-2026. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

`SKILL.md` says how to label an answer drawn from these files.
